The Mg-rich phases (MgO, Mg-rich antimonates) have gaps that are too wide. Measured EQE rose from 0.0025% at index 20 (Sb 0.58) to 0.0176% at index 25 (Sb 0.73). It then dipped slightly to 0.0147% at index 26 (Sb 0.76), so the peak is at or near index 25.

content.text:
I've finished the campaign and submitted **index 25 (Mg 0.27 / Sb 0.73)** as the best composition. Its EQE is about 0.018%, a very small value in absolute terms.

I only had three merit measurements. The known phases suggested that only Sb-rich films, with Sb in a lower or mixed oxidation state, would absorb the 3.2 eV light. Mg-rich films should have band gaps too wide to absorb it. So I spent all three measurements on the Sb-rich end:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | 0.58 | 0.0025 |
| 25 | 0.73 | 0.0176 |
| 26 | 0.76 | 0.0147 |

EQE rose steeply toward the Sb-rich end and dropped slightly at the very edge, so the peak is at or near index 25.

- **Mg-rich half not measured:** I rejected indices 0–19 because of their expected wide band gaps. I didn't test that assumption directly, so it's the main risk to the result.
- **XRD not used:** I didn't spend any of the five XRD measurements. The phases I've linked to the high-EQE films are assumptions from the phase list, not confirmed.
- **Neighbours not measured:** Indices 21–24 were never measured. A value slightly above index 25's could be hiding there, most likely at index 24.
